findings.inspection_type: Known-issue reproduction applied to a current unconditional claim
findings.title: Sharing only gradients does not ensure data privacy/security
findings.source_location: Section4.2 p7, federated-learning paragraph and healthcare example
findings.claim: Local raw data and shared updates ensure privacy/security and regulatory compliance.
findings.suspect_step: Data locality is treated as sufficient for confidentiality of released updates.

counterexample.assumptions: One-record client gradient, known model, visible individual gradient/update, no added protection stipulated; raw record remains local
counterexample.stated_result: Confidentiality would be ensured by retaining raw record locally

historical_attribution.authors: Ligeng Zhu; Zhijian Liu; Song Han
historical_attribution.title: Deep Leakage from Gradients

findings.counterevidence: Later sections recognize risks but supply no protective mechanism. Properly protected FL may offer specific guarantees; not every FL update is reconstructible.
findings.supported_impact: Minor retained because the error concerns an application-enabling assurance on one branch of the architecture, rather than a derivation or necessary generalization establishing the proposed scaling axes. The automatic privacy/security assurance and resulting compliance inference must be withdrawn.

repair.statement: FL can avoid raw-data centralization; confidentiality/security depend on threat model, visible messages and added protections; compliance does not follow from FL alone.
repair.verified: Logical wording correction; no full secure protocol implemented or certified

severity_calibration.core_dependency: Section4.1 defines Scaling Out through specialized foundation-model variants and connecting interfaces. Section4.2 offers federated learning alongside parameter-efficient adaptation, conditional control and system-level protocols. The false confidentiality implication supports suitability of one route for sensitive healthcare data; specialization, interoperation and distributed-training capability are not derived from that implication.
assumptions_rechecked: The saved example has one-record client data, a known model and a visible individual gradient/update
The residual is nonzero and no protective transformation is stipulated
Raw data remains local, so the example satisfies the paper's stated locality premise
counterevidence_and_survivors: Later risk acknowledgments do not supply a protection excluding the example.
Protected FL protocols can differ; the check does not characterize a deployed hospital system.
Collaboration without centralizing raw records remains an architectural capability, not a confidentiality guarantee for the released messages.

known_issue_reproduction.scope: Reviewer toy analytic example, not execution of original attack

scope_clarifications: Research roadmap is not a proven required sequence
Trainable state, active compute and stored parameters differ
Prospective blockchain and ecosystem benefits need protocol-specific/empirical evaluation
